canonical_fact: Safrole is JAM's stateful block-production mechanism, derived from a simplified Sassafras design, that assigns block-authoring opportunity by timeslot.
misconceptions: Safrole is JAM’s data-availability protocol rather than its block-production mechanism.
title: Safrole

canonical_fact: For each epoch Safrole determines a sequence with one sealing entry per potential block timeslot.
title: Slot-sealer sequence

canonical_fact: A Safrole ticket combines a verifiably random ticket identifier with an entry index and anonymously represents a validator's claim to a timeslot.
misconceptions: A Safrole ticket publicly reveals the validator identity that submitted it.

relations.statement: Candidate tickets are collected in the ticket accumulator before selection for a later slot-sealer sequence.

title: Safrole ticket

canonical_fact: The ticket identifier is an unbiasable deterministic RingVRF output used to score and select Safrole tickets without directly revealing the validator identity.
title: Ticket identifier

canonical_fact: The ticket accumulator retains the highest-scoring candidate tickets from the current contest for use in the next epoch.
title: Ticket accumulator

canonical_fact: Safrole uses Bandersnatch RingVRF proofs so a validator can prove membership in the validator key set while producing a verifiable random output without revealing which validator key was used.

relations.statement: RingVRF output provides the anonymous verifiable ticket identifier.

title: Bandersnatch RingVRF

canonical_fact: The active validator set contains validator keys currently privileged to author blocks and perform validation duties.
misconceptions: The active validator set is identical to the staging set at all times.
title: Active validator set

canonical_fact: The staging validator set is the prospective sequence from which later validator sets are formed.
title: Staging validator set

canonical_fact: The pending validator set is reset from the staging set at an epoch boundary and is intended to become active in the following epoch.
title: Pending validator set

canonical_fact: JAM retains the previous validator key set alongside the active and prospective sets for protocol operations that need recent validator history.
title: Previous validator set

canonical_fact: A validator key record contains Bandersnatch, Ed25519 and BLS public keys plus validator metadata.
title: Validator key tuple

canonical_fact: A null validator key is an intentionally invalid validator key tuple used to disable an offender from participating after key rotation.
misconceptions: The null validator key is a normal key whose private key is held by governance.
title: Null validator key

canonical_fact: At epoch transitions JAM rotates pending, active and previous validator sets and filters incoming offender keys to the null key.

relations.statement: Epoch rotation advances pending keys into the active validator set.

title: Validator key rotation

canonical_fact: Each block folds the VRF output from the header into an entropy accumulator, with historical epoch values retained for later protocol randomness.

relations.statement: The block entropy VRF output is folded into the protocol entropy accumulator.

title: Entropy accumulator

canonical_fact: If the normal ticket contest does not adequately populate the next epoch's ticket sequence, Safrole can use a fallback slot-sealer sequence based on validator keys.
title: Fallback sealing
